title: Denormalizing Many-to-Many Relationships in a Document Model (IMS Mistake)
pattern: Embedding/denormalizing many-to-many relationships directly as nested sub-documents inside a document database.
why_bad: It duplicates shared data, leading to inconsistency when the shared record (e.g. Organization's address) is updated. This repeats the hierarchical database mistakes of the 1960s.
detection: A document database schema where non-tree, many-to-many relationships are embedded as nested array values.
counterexample: Embedding strict one-to-many tree structures where child elements are owned exclusively by a single parent document.
fix: Store reference IDs instead of nested objects, and perform client-side or database-level lookup resolution.
